section_bounds_rule: A census row's label is accepted on a page only if its top lies between the top of its OWN section's heading (the census section title found on that page as a contiguous word run, the same exact-word matching _find_label uses, topmost occurrence, less ROW_TOL) and the top (less ROW_TOL) of the nearest OTHER census section's heading that sits below it on that page, or the page bottom when none does; a heading on the same text row as this one does not close the bounds. If the section's own heading is not on the page, that (row, page) search is the unchanged whole-page search and is counted in heading_fallbacks. The switch is the module flag extract.SECTION_BOUNDS (default True; False restores the old whole-page search). The page order, _row_values, the date rules and the section id format are untouched.
how_counted: extract.extract(..., stats=<dict>) fills stats['heading_fallbacks'] (one per (row, page) search whose section heading is not on the page) and stats['bounded_searches'] (one per (row, page) search inside bounds). stats is not part of the result, so the result is byte-identical.

heading_fallbacks_detail.unit: (census row, page) searches made while extracting the 4 existing fixtures, whole-page search used because the row's section heading is not on that page
